title: Inventory.remove lets stock go negative
body: `Inventory.remove(id, quantity)` happily drives stock below zero (e.g. removing 5 when 2 are in stock leaves -3). It should throw a `RangeError` when the quantity is not a positive integer or exceeds the current stock, and it must leave the stock unchanged in that case.
plan:
Validate remove() quantity and prevent negative stock: throw RangeError for invalid quantities (non-positive integer or exceeding current stock) and leave stock unchanged. This fixes bug where removing more than available produced negative stock.
1. Validate quantity and prevent negative stock in remove()
requirements: Inventory.remove(id, quantity) throws RangeError when quantity is not a positive integer
Inventory.remove(id, quantity) throws RangeError when quantity exceeds current stock
When RangeError is thrown, the book's stock must remain unchanged
Existing behavior: removing valid quantity still decrements stock and returns the book
Removing a non-existent book still throws Error(`Unknown book: ${id}`) (unchanged)
No other public APIs or tests are altered
summary:
Tightened validation in Inventory.remove to enforce positive integer quantity and prevent removing more than available stock. Implementation throws RangeError for non-positive-integer quantity and when quantity exceeds current stock, leaving stock unchanged in those cases. Existing behavior for valid removals and unknown book errors unchanged. Verified by running npm test: all inventory-related tests pass; the test suite still has one unrelated pre-existing failure in math.divide (divide by zero test), which was not modified.

Requirements:
1. R1. Inventory.remove throws RangeError when quantity is not a positive integer (src/inventory.js: remove)
2. R2. Inventory.remove throws RangeError when quantity exceeds current stock (src/inventory.js: remove)
3. R3. When RangeError is thrown, the book's stock remains unchanged (logic checks before decrement in src/inventory.js: remove)
4. R4. Removing valid quantity still decrements stock and returns the book (src/inventory.js: remove)
5. R5. Removing a non-existent book still throws Error(`Unknown book: ${id}`) (src/inventory.js: remove)
6. R6. No other public APIs or tests were altered (only src/inventory.js changed)
verify: npm test --silent: exit before=1 after=1; no new test failures
